title: Siblings Neighbourhood Effects
author: Lina Hedman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.z6af9ae

steps.title: Identify Initial Study Population
steps.instruction: Filter individuals from the IBF_IndData1990_2014.dta dataset who were aged 15-21 in 1990.

substeps.instruction: Calculate age in 1990 using birth year (FoddAr).
Keep individuals where 15 <= age <= 21.
Retain variables: IBFLopNr, IBFLopNrMor, IBFLopNrFar, sex, and FoddAr.

steps.title: Determine Parental Home Residency and Departure
steps.instruction: Identify individuals living with parents in 1990 and determine the year they left the parental home.

substeps.instruction: Merge family IDs (FamLopNr) from annual files (ibf_bef) for the child, mother, and father for years 1990-2010.
Identify those living with parents in 1990 (FamLopNr1990 matches mother or father's FamLopNr1990).
Determine the first year of leaving the parental home (yrleavehome) between 1991 and 1997 by checking when the child's FamLopNr no longer matches the parents'.
Keep only individuals who moved out between 1991 and 1997.
Calculate yrleave_14 (yrleavehome + 13).
Categorize which parent the individual lived with before moving (1=mother, 2=father, 3=both).

steps.title: Construct Real Sibling Pairs
steps.instruction: Create same-sex sibling pairs based on shared parents and specific age/departure criteria.

substeps.instruction: Split the dataset into separate files for boys and girls.
Identify siblings by grouping by IBFLopNrMor and IBFLopNrFar.
Filter for siblings with an age difference <= 3 years.
Filter for families where at least one child left home between 1991 and 1993.
Filter for siblings who left home within 4 years of each other (leave_diff <= 4).
Keep only the pair closest in age and those who lived with the same parent.
Assign unique sibling IDs (2,000,000+ for females, 1,000,000+ for males) and merge into a single population file.

steps.title: Enrich Individual Data
steps.instruction: Merge comprehensive socio-economic and geographic data for the selected individuals.

substeps.instruction: Merge basic data (Fland, FlandFar) and recode father's country of birth (cob_father) into 4 categories: Sweden, Western, Eastern Europe/Russia, and Africa/Asia/South America.
Calculate annual age from 1990 to 2010.
Merge neighborhood IDs (sams/SAMSomrade) for 1990-2010.
Merge LISA data (Sun2000Niva, SyssStatJ, FamTypF) and recode into education (edu), employment (emp), couple status (couple), and children in household (child_hh).
Merge income data (ForvErs) for 1990-2010, adjust for inflation using specific yearly KPI divisors (e.g., 1991/1.09, 2010/1.46), and create logged income variables (ln_inc).
Merge tenure data (IBFFastLopNr, Typkod, JurFormGrp) and recode into tenure categories (1=home ownership, 2=cooperative, 3=rental).

steps.title: Generate Neighborhood Income Data
steps.instruction: Calculate the share of low-income earners in each neighborhood (SAMS) per year.

substeps.instruction: For each year (1990-2010), identify individuals of working age (20-64).
Determine the 30th and 70th percentiles of income (forvers) for the working-age population.
Flag individuals as low-income (below 30th percentile) or high-income (above 70th percentile).
Collapse data by SAMS to calculate the share of low-income earners (sh_low = numlow / total working age * 100).
Merge these annual neighborhood shares back into the main individual dataset.

steps.title: Construct Random Sibling Pairs
steps.instruction: Generate a control group of random pairs matched on neighborhood, sex, father's birth country, and father's income level.

substeps.instruction: Filter individuals born 1969-1975 and determine their 1990 residency and departure year.
Categorize father's 1990 income (inc_fa): 1 (< 878), 2 (878-1609), 3 (>= 1610).
Randomly pair individuals within the same 1990 SAMS, sex, cob_father, and inc_fa group.
Filter random pairs to match real sibling criteria: at least one leaves home 1991-1993, leave_diff <= 4, and age_diff <= 3.
Remove any pairs that are actually related (shared mother or father).
Merge random pairs with the real sibling dataset, marking them as siblingtype 0.

steps.title: Prepare Panel Data for Analysis
steps.instruction: Transform the dataset into a panel format and calculate cumulative neighborhood effects.

substeps.instruction: Reshape data to long format (by year).
Identify the neighborhood of the parents at the time the child left home (sams_par).
Keep only the window from the year of leaving home to 14 years later.
Calculate 'yrsinceleave' as the sequence of years after departure.
Calculate average income (inc_av) for the 12th-14th years since leaving.
Calculate the cumulative share of low-income neighbors (shlow_cum) from year 1 to year 11.
Keep only the observation for year 11 since leaving.
Calculate family mean (fammean_shlowc) and intra-family deviation (intrafammean_shlowc) for the cumulative share.

steps.title: Perform Statistical Analysis
steps.instruction: Run descriptive statistics and mixed-effects models to analyze the impact of neighborhood income on individual income.

substeps.instruction: Run descriptives for inc_av, shlow_cum, and demographics, split by sibling type and sex.
Execute mixed-effects models (xi:mixed) for males and females, comparing real vs. random siblings.
Include covariates: age, cob_father, couple, child_hh, edu, emp, and tenure.
Use random effects for the parental neighborhood (sams_par) and family ID (famID).
